newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty idles vs basket, eyes dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty idles vs basket, eyes dlr/mark.

text.p: The Polish zloty drifted idly against the basket of currencies as the market focused on dollar/mark changes on world markets, dealer said.
They said the immediate threat of a central bank currency buying intervention faded on Tuesday as the zloty found a comfort zone between 3.05 and 3.10 percent from parity.
"The present zloty level doesn't seem to bother anyone... and the market seems set to track dollar/mark for the rest of the day," said Katarzyna Solerz, dealer at Pekao SA.
At 0855 GMT the zloty was at 3.11/3.07 percent from parity, just up from opening and flat from Monday's 3.09/3.06 close.

The zloty was at 3.1280/90 to the dollar, up from 3.1290/00 at opening but lower than Monday's 3.1198/08 after the U.S. unit's overnight rise. It was at 1.8076/82 to the mark, up from opening at 1.8084/94 and yesterday's close at 1.8110/15.

Dealers said the central bank was not likely to intervene against the zloty as long as the local unit drifted around present levels because such a move could cause an inflow of speculative foreign capital, hoping for a zloty rise.
Dealers said the estimated $40 million worth foreign investor purchases of Polish T-bills at Monday's auction is not likely to cause much upward pressure on the zloty on Tuesday.

On the money market spread of one-day deposits widened after the central bank announced a 200 million zloty NBP-bill sale and a 100 million zloty reverse repo on Tuesday, but rates remained anchored below 23 percent, dealers said.
At 0920 GMT overnight rates were quoted at 22.55/22.95 percent against 22.70/22.95 percent at 0630 GMT.
Tomorrow/next rates were at 22.65/22.85 percent, just down from 22.75/22.95 percent at opening.
